messages.author: 91b36e77d3ed48b5
messages.subject: validity of pcountOpen model results?
parts:
Hi unmarked community,
First, let me say how thankful I am for this google group. I'm new to occupancy modeling, and I'm SO glad there's a group like this to lean on for advice! 

Before I understood the importance of accounting for imperfect detection and observer error in the analysis of point count data, I used the rstanarm package to model whether my song playback experiments resulted in an increase in black-and-white warbler abundance at survey stops receiving treatment as compared to control stops. I used year-to-year changes in naive abundance to model a binary response of increase vs. no increase. I conducted this experiment across three different sites that varied in habitat quality, and I also measure forest understory vegetation cover, which has been shown to be important habitat requirement for this species. Below I've included some results from a logistic rstanarm model in which playback treatment was the only predictor that had uncertainty intervals that didn't include zero.    


BAWW Increase in Abundance

Predictors         Log-Odds Uncertainty Intervals (95%)
siteBunp                          0.13 -2.69 – 3.14
siteFss                          2.58 -0.16 – 5.67
siteSgla                          0.74 -2.18 – 3.91
control                          0.35 -2.71 – 3.83
playback                          3.29 0.47 – 6.84
understoryVeg                  0.02 -0.64 – 0.66







I've tried modeling these data in unmarked, and the effect of playback treatment is no longer important. Because I'm so new to unmarked, I don't know if this result is valid or if I've coded something wrong. In the model summary, the effect of playback treatments on recruitment is slightly negative, which doesn't seem to make sense given how the naive abundance changed in the raw data. 

I'm using the pcountOpen function with the following parameters:
M = 37 sites
T = 3 years
J = up to 5 surveys per year 


Treatment changed across years, so I've included it as yearlySiteCovs.
Understory vegetation cover and site ID are siteCovs. 
Whether each survey was conducted during the early-season prospecting period or late-season breeding period was included as obsCovs.

During year 1, I collected data on the initial abundance of my species at all sites (I want to model changes in abundance based on these data).
Years 2 and 3 were experimental seasons during which some sites were exposed to long-term playback treatments to test whether those treatments would result in recruitment. 
For the primaryPeriod argument I specified one column for each year (1,2,3) of M length. 

Please see my code and output below, and I'm attaching my data csv. If anyone could help me understand whether these results are valid or not, I would GREATLY appreciate it. I just don't know if this model is actually testing my question: Did playbacks have an effect on recruitment? Additionally, I want to know whether there is an interaction between treatment and site ID, but when I run that model, I get the Hessian singularity error. Not sure how to approach adding start values to address that issue. 

Thanks in advance! 
 
Sincerely, 
Justin   



SI.df <- read.csv("bawwPCountOpen.csv", h=T)

treat <- as.matrix(SI.df[,17:19])
season <- as.matrix(SI.df[,23:37])

?unmarkedFramePCO()

y.baww <- SI.df[2:16] #count of male black-and-white warblers within 100m
                      #of survey point [0,1,2] (zero inflated?)
TreatByYear <- as.matrix(SI.df[17:19]) #Site and Year specific treatment (baseline=initial occupancy, control, playback)
CovBySite <- SI.df[38:39] #Site ID and Understory Vegetation Cover 
SeasonByObs <- as.matrix(SI.df[23:37]) #season (prospect or breeding)
prim<- as.matrix(SI.df[20:22]) #primary period, year: 1,2,3 M*T

umfPCO <- unmarkedFramePCO(y = y.baww, siteCovs = CovBySite, 
                           yearlySiteCovs = list(Treat=TreatByYear),
                           obsCovs = list(Season=SeasonByObs),
                           numPrimary = 3, primaryPeriod = prim)
summary(umfPCO)
?pcountOpen

#####Null model#####
m0 <- pcountOpen(lambdaformula = ~1, #initial abundance
                 gammaformula = ~1, #recruitment rate
                 omegaformula = ~1, #survival prob
                 pformula = ~1, #detection prob
                 data = umfPCO,
                 mixture = "ZIP", #zeroinflation?
                 K = 25,
                 dynamics = "constant", #constant (no expected relationship between omega & gamma)
                 se = TRUE)
summary(m0)

m1 <- pcountOpen(lambdaformula = ~1, 
                 gammaformula = ~Treat, 
                 omegaformula = ~1, 
                 pformula = ~1, 
                 data = umfPCO,
                 mixture = "ZIP", 
                 K = 25,
                 dynamics = "trend", 
                 se = TRUE)

summary(m1)




Call:
pcountOpen(lambdaformula = ~1, gammaformula = ~Treat, omegaformula = ~1, 
    pformula = ~1, data = umfPCO, mixture = "ZIP", K = 25, 
    dynamics = "trend", se = TRUE)

Abundance (log-scale):
 Estimate    SE   z  P(>|z|)
     2.11 0.619 3.4 0.000664

Growth Rate (log-scale):
              Estimate    SE      z P(>|z|)
(Intercept)     0.1223 0.195  0.626   0.531
TreatPlayback  -0.0843 0.277 -0.305   0.761

Detection (logit-scale):
 Estimate    SE     z  P(>|z|)
    -3.12 0.558 -5.59 2.22e-08

Zero-inflation (logit-scale):
 Estimate    SE     z P(>|z|)
    -1.01 0.574 -1.75    0.08

AIC: 278.0295 
Number of sites: 37
optim convergence code: 0
optim iterations: 54 
Bootstrap iterations: 0

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] validity of pcountOpen model results?
parts:
hi Justin,
 I would recommend against using the Dail-Madsen model for this purpose. There is too much additional model structure that makes formulating and testing the specific hypotheses difficult.  If you want a detection-adjusted model I would recommend using the simple N-mixture model on the stacked data (this has been discussed on the email list before). But the idea is to take the data from each year (a m atrix) and then stack the year-specific matrices on top of each other so that Ystacked = [Y1, Y2, Y3]'  and then use the pcount function. Effectively it treats each site/year combination as a new site. Then you can create a site effect "treatment" and test that directly. I would recommend a nonparametric bootstrap to improve the SE estimation. If you did this model in JAGS then I would use a random effect for the sites across years to account for that dependence, but you can't do that in unmarked. If you email me off the list here I can send you a draft chapter from the AHM2 book which talks about stacking and also using the nonparametric bootstrap.
regards
andy
